action: Frame-limit investigation: NO 6-frame cap exists; caps are 8 (public/kid_safe per scene) / 60 (private per scene) / 40 scenes
details: server.js:1542,1546,5000-5004 enforce; the only '6's are LAYER caps (MAX_ROOM_LAYERS=6 paint, 3 anim). Production verified: happypaint-app-1 has NO anim/frame env overrides -> runs defaults. FLIPBOOK (public animation room) on disk: scenes=1, frames=8/8 = FULL, hostless so scene_add is refused (server.js:4917) -> a visitor today can add ZERO frames; frame duration default 120ms (~8fps). Cost model: frame record is cheap, cost scales with frames x ops; animation rooms are excluded from the gzip join cache (server.js:2228) and from snapshots (server.js:1166), so every join stringifies all ops synchronously; op budget MAX_ANIM_ROOM_OPS=120000 rejects past that (~266 ops/frame at 450 frames). Export is already memory-flat (videoExport.js:9-10). Routes: (1) film timing (holds/loops/cameras) = 30s from 8-60 cels, zero code; (2) confined per-cel film store outside room.history (450+); (3) raise private cap + gzip-cache variant; (4) animation doc at 1600x1000 (their 'restrict animation mode' permission); (5) FLIPBOOK auto-rollover so the public room isn't dead.
outcome: reported to owner; awaiting the anishare teardown before proposing the build order

action: Diagnosed and fixed the studio's dead + : committed e4c7395
details: Reproduced: room started with 2 cels, taps added one cel each up to 8, then the + was disabled with title 'Loops are capped at 8 frames'. Two bugs: (1) the + is the LAST item inside the horizontally scrolling .fs-reel, so once cels overflow it scrolls off-screen — the tap lands on empty strip; nothing scrolled the reel either; (2) at the cap the + was disabled → zero feedback (no toast, no tooltip on tablet), and the copy said 'loops' instead of cels. Also found and fixed in my own first attempt: aria-disabled makes Playwright/assistive tech treat the control as not-actionable. Fixes: + pinned sticky right, reel scrolls active cel into view, + never disabled and explains the cap with host/guest-specific copy, label carries the count. Verified: scripts/frame-cap-verify.mjs (new), filmstrip-verify 13/13, film-timing-verify 26/26.
outcome: shipped; the user's '6' was visible-cel counting on a scrolling reel, not a cap
